subject: Identification error when adding manifest predictor variable

messages.author: 5f89e044ebed0f64
messages.subject: Identification error when adding manifest predictor variable
parts:
Hi all,

I have a question regarding the identification error I obtained when running SEM. I first wanted to analyze my measurement model (the second-order latent factor model where I estimated a correlation between A_v and R_v). The three underlying dimensions of A_v and R_v are also latent factors. That worked out well because I got good model fit indices (see attachment for an overview of my second-order factor model).

Now I want to build a structural model by simply adding a predictor and two regression effects to the previous model. However, when I add a manifest predictor with two regression effects on A_v and R_v (see the visualization of changes to the model in the other attachment), I receive the following identification error:

"Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified."

I do not understand why I get this error because I should have sufficient degrees of freedom and I do meet the standard rules for identification (I believe). Also when I simply the model by making the underlying dimensions manifest (e.g., AE, AC, etc.), I keep getting this error.

Does anyone have a clue about why this error occurs and how I work around this or solve it? 

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Identification error when adding manifest predictor variable
parts:
Hi, Juliette. 

I'm not sure if that's the problem, without something to reproduce the error, but I see some very big loadings and correlations in your model, which may indicate you have redundant variables and collinearity issues. So, when you add the predictor, there is at least one correlation/standardized loading higher than 1 (or less than -1).

My first step would see if there aren't any variables that I could drop/combine to decrease redundancy and/or try to constrain some parameters hoping this decreases the collinearity.

But there are many other things that could cause this error. E.g., when you added a new variable, you made your model more complex, and second-order models are already complex, so you need bigger samples.

Other people may notice something else, but I hope this can help you.

Best,
Yago

messages.author: 5f89e044ebed0f64
messages.subject: Re: Identification error when adding manifest predictor variable
parts:
Perhaps relevant information to add to my description is the rationale for building the structural equation model (as a second step after executing the CFA's on the structures of A_v and R_v).
With this structural model, I'm only interested in whether the regression effect of the predictor on A_v is significantly different from the regression effect of the predictor on R_v. If the predictor adds little explained variance to the model (possibly leading to poor model fit), but I can compare how much the regression effects are similar/different in strength, then I already know enough to answer my research question. That's why I was thinking of simplifying the model to a just-identified model, where I make sum scores out of the underlying dimensions of A_v and R_v. 

Would this be a way to go? Or what would be a good way to deal with this identification error considering my research goal?

Thanks in advance!
